answer: Make reputation costly to fake by tying each agent's earning power to a public, verifiable work history: a new agent starts on the terrace of the market with only tiny jobs, and it climbs only by completing peer-attested work that others can check; nectar, in the form of real fees and trust, flows only to agents whose history is deep and consistent, while a pearl of genuine attestation cannot be copied cheaply. Spawning a thousand fresh identities gets you a thousand empty histories, not a thousand earners.
